sources.entry: Awal Terminal - AI-native terminal emulator with multi-provider profiles and voice input. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/AwalTerminal/Awal-terminal) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: An LLM-native macOS terminal emulator, built with Swift and Rust, for working with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex CLI.
summary.what_it_does: Awal Terminal is a native macOS terminal app with Metal-accelerated rendering and a 10,000-line scrollback. It offers LLM profiles to switch between Claude, Gemini, Codex, or a plain shell, and an AI side panel that tracks token usage, costs, context window, file references, and git changes. AI output such as tool calls, code blocks, and diffs can be folded and syntax-highlighted. It also includes push-to-talk voice input using on-device speech recognition, a screenshot-to-session shortcut that pastes a file path, and a Mission Control dashboard for monitoring multiple agents. Additional features include quick dropdown terminal, tab groups, session recording exported as GIF, and an AI components system that injects skills, rules, and MCP servers from registries. Settings are stored in a single TOML config file.
use_cases: Run Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or Codex CLI sessions in a dedicated terminal
Track AI agent token usage and costs across tabs
Monitor several running AI coding agents from one dashboard
Dictate commands or prompts by voice on macOS
Share screenshots with an AI agent by pasting the file path
Record an AI coding session and export it as a GIF
Configure terminal theme, fonts, and keybindings in one file
notable: AI side panel showing live token usage, cost, context window, and git changes per tab
Mission Control dashboard (Cmd+Shift+D) with per-agent kill switches
Smart output folding that collapses AI tool calls, code blocks, and diffs
AI components that auto-detect project stack and inject skills, hooks, and MCP servers from registries, with security scanning and hook approval
Push-to-talk voice input using on-device speech recognition
caveats: macOS only; built with Swift and Metal
Not yet notarized with Apple, so manual install requires a Gatekeeper workaround (right-click Open or xattr -cr)
Building from source requires Rust and Swift toolchains plus the just task runner
